text_fidelity_a:
GoPro Hero — Waterproof Digital Action Camera for Travel with Touch Screen 1080p HD Video 10MP Photos Battery life is not bad. It works better as something that you turn on, capture the action and then shut off rather than allowing it to record until the battery level causes a shut down. 1080 / 60 is the lowest setting you can get on this. Another thing is that the system on it won't give you 1 large file, even with recording without any breaks for say 20 minutes that results in 3 different files on the SD card of about 4 to 5 gigabytes per file. Yeah.. Get as large of SD card you can. I think it supports up to 128Gig. Moving said large files from the SD to computer.. even with USB3 takes a while.
Water resistance hasn't been an issue. I seem to remember that it's good down to like 45 foot or something but our use hasn't been anything deeper than 12 feet.
With all the negatives, this is still a decent deal considering water resistance, and HD being base quality of recording.
text_fidelity_b: GoPro Hero — Waterproof Digital Action Camera for Travel with Touch Screen 1080p HD Video 10MP Photos

text_fidelity_a:
MIATONE Outdoor Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speaker Wireless - Green When I first opened the box, I kind of doubted that this compact bluetooth speaker was worth $50. But, after I got it fully charged (which didn't take long) and connected to my phone (super easy), I opened my graphic equalizer app and then started my favorite Pandora station. I cannot say enough about how surprised and pleased I am about the sound quality! The bass is thumping! The treble is crisp and clear! I have other BT speakers this size and none of them even come close to the quality! This Miatone TWS BT speaker is awesome!

Note: because the sound comes out both sides and both ends, you need to keep the control panel at the top (or the bottom). Otherwise, you lose some of the sound quality. So, propping it up in the right position is essential to getting the best quality sound.

I had to knock off one star on the portability factor for one thing; it's a perfect cylinder with no flat edge to keep it from rolling away. And, placing it on end will muffle part of the bass, as both ends have that wonderful bass speaker in them. I guess you can make sure that you place it either on a perfectly flat surface or if it's on a slope, that the included cord is underneath like a 'wheel chock'. But, overall, that's just a minor oversight. I still have to give this amazing little BOOMBOX five stars, because of the quality of construction and the amazing sound. I have JBL's this size that don't sound as good. Super happy with this purchase. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: MIATONE Outdoor Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speaker Wireless - Green

Vantec NexStar Gx USB 3.1 Gen 2 Type-C 2.5” SATA SSD/HDD Enclosure for 9.5mm & 7mm Height Drive; Comes with C to C and C to A Cable; Aluminum Casing; (NST-271C31-BK) I was replacing the hard drive in my laptop and wanted an enclosure for the old one. I saw that this one was cheap and had mostly positive reviews, so I thought I'd take a chance on it. With free super saver shipping, it arrived in about a week and a half and it was exactly as I expected it would be from reading the reviews. It is true what several of the reviews have mentioned, the screws that come with it truly do not hold the end cap in the case (which means that the hard drive can slip in and out). It was a fairly simple fix; I just had to find some other screws that actually held it together. Another thing that's been mentioned is that there is no way to turn the enclosure off, i.e. if the drive is plugged into the computer it will be on regardless of if the computer is on or not (at least in my experience).

Conclusion: A good product if you need/want a hard drive enclosure and don't want to spend a lot. Having to find different screws and not being able to turn the drive off without unplugging it from the computer keep it from being five stars.

That's my two cents.
text_fidelity_b: Vantec NexStar Gx USB 3.1 Gen 2 Type-C 2.5” SATA SSD/HDD Enclosure for 9.5mm & 7mm Height Drive; Comes with C to C and C to A Cable; Aluminum Casing; (NST-271C31-BK)

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung 32GB up to 48MB/s EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC Card with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM) Deciding to catch up on my product reviews – I was ELATED this particular Micro sD card is no longer available. I know that’s a bit mean-spirited, but I can’t help it. I was out the money for the item because it was past Amazon’s 30-day return window.

I purchased one in October of 2015 for my Samsung GS4, and only two (2) months later – I needed a brand new one. Why? It failed. No warning, nothing. Just a failure.

And this wouldn’t be the first failure either.

The sD card I bought in December failed as well, but I’ll give it up for it – It went OVER three (3) years before failing. It failed April 3, 2019. I remember that because of the event it failed during. I would’ve expected the failure when I transferred the sD card from the S4 to the S8 in May 2018, but the card still worked.

There were no signs of pending failure or issues. The night before (4/2), it worked and I was able to retrieve some photos off of it.

My mother and I went to Knott’s Berry Farm for the Boysenberry Festival. And, any photos take before we left – GONE. No error messages – just gone. I didn’t know until I got home.

What photos I have were the return photos from the drive home. I had briefly
glanced at the card data (on my phone) at about 2pm, but after that (without being dropped, banged, over-heated) the card failed. I know some will ask why I didn’t back them up – I was in transit, driving on the freeway, so it wasn’t feasible.

All I know is that my photos were gone.

So, I had to purchase another sD card for my phone. This time I chose the GREEN Evo Select one. And, from April 2019 to the date of this review, it’s been pretty solid. Though I’m not taking any chances. I store photos to my S8 as well as the sD card.

Since it isn’t available, I won’t bother with saying I don’t recommend it. I certainly won’t buy it again if it does become available again.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 32GB up to 48MB/s EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC Card with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM)

text_fidelity_a:
Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I'm a software developer who works in a cubicle world with the heating system droning on above the ceiling (we're on the top floor of an office building - the HVAC is on the roof). These headphones provide an oasis of silence! The noise cancellation *seems* to be a cut above the others I've tried (Beats Studio at Target and a Sony set at Costco) although it's not really fair to compare as I didn't try the Bose under the same condition as the others (i.e. in a noisy store).

How good is it? The droning AC noise is completely gone. Voices I can still hear - until I play music. Even at low/moderate playback volume, voices are barely audible. People have to pat me on the back if they want my attention.

Comfort is excellent. I wear them on-and-off all day without problems. I imagine people with big ears might be less comfortable.

Power: the headphones use a single AAA battery. Keeping in mind that I maybe play music for 2-3 hours every day, the battery seems to last 2-3 weeks. As others have noted, these headphones will not work (i.e. play music) without power.

My one nitpick (and the reason I can't give it 5 stars) is the god-awful chord. It's some cheap plasticky material that I continually have to unravel by dangling the headphones by the plug end and letting the headphones rotate. It's really quite pathetic to put such cheap cr$p on $300 headphones - shame on Bose for not correcting this. Is it really going to affect your profitability so much you can't do something like the $20 Apple headphones that come with every iPhone (they're more rubberized and don't seem to get raveled).

Update for iPhone/iPad/iPod users: with iOS 7, Apple introduced a new way to invoke Siri (Apple's voice assistant) - instead of holding down the home button (or center button on the headphones) until you hear the Siri confirmation sound and then asking Siri your question and then waiting for Siri to accept your input, with iOS 7, you can keep the button pressed until you're finished talking - and avoid the delay Siri normally waits to know you're done with talking. It's a very useful feature.....and, it doesn't work with the Bose inline chord button :-( Not really Bose's fault, I guess, but I thought it worth mentioning.
text_fidelity_b: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models) Overall, this is a fine case for the 8.9 inch Fire HD. The overall quality is quite nice - I have other Marware products for my Kindle Touch, and it's good to see that they are continuing to maintain a strong focus on product quality. All the materials feel nice; the stitching is tight and even; there's ample cushioning for tablet protection while maintaining a slim profile; and the elastic strap holds the cover closed in a secure fashion.

I also like how Marware packages their products with a minimum of packaging waste but still ensures the product can travel through the mail without being dinged up. The package is also easy to open - no fuss, no muss.

I initially had some difficulty getting the Fire into the case. The Fire is held in place using a plastic cradle, but it seemed to be too small. I had to (gasp!) resort to reading the user guide that came with it, and found out I needed to position it in a certain way and then snap it in. When it is properly inserted you'll hear and feel a clear "snap" at each of the four corners of the tablet. When properly installed the case holds the tablet very securely. I shook it vigorously (over a thick cushion in case it failed) and the Fire stayed put.

My main quibble is with the rotation feature. I was really looking forward to this since some apps only run in portrait mode; others only in landscape. While the rotation feature works, it is very stiff - you really have to twist hard to get it to rotate. It's a two-handed operation: one hand to rotate the tablet; the other to hold the case while you're turning.

The bottom of the cradle has a tab that fits into a slot on the base of the cover to prop up the tablet. This works in both landscape and portrait modes. There are three tabs so you can adjust the angle.

There are cut outs for the power and HDMI ports. I had no problems accessing any of the ports, power button or volume controls while it was in the cover.

Since I often end up having to charge the Fire while it is in use, I rotated the screen so the power plug is at the top. That allows me to keep the tablet propped up on my desk in landscape mode for video watching, but still use the power cord.

It also offers an auto on/off ability - the Fire turns off when you close the cover, and wakes up when you open the cover. It's a nice feature and it works well.

It has a slot on the cover so you can fit your hand into it for ease of holding it. That has value, but what I would have preferred to have instead (or in addition to) is a pocket on either the inside or the outside to hold items such as a cleaning cloth. text_fidelity_a:
TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions I was so excited to finally have a separate GPS again, as my Garmin one was from 2009 (OLD maps) and using my phone was unsafe because even with stuff disabled during driving, I was still getting messages and interruptions that would pop up, plus I like listening to something on the drive, and using it as a GPS makes that tricky. Having tried several Garmin models, Apple Maps, and Google Maps, I was excited to try TomTom. And I was disappointed.

Problems:
•Screen is VERY dim in the sunlight, and living in Florida, this is most of the time. It is NOT easy to see the map, which even in my ancient Garmin is much more visible and automatically switches from day mode to night mode. Likewise, my iPhone screen automatically changes brightness for the amount of sun coming in. And this? It looks horribly dim and takes a lot of effort to see.
•Routes don’t always make sense. I’m used to some amount of this in the other systems I’ve tried, but they’re really wacky on this thing, taking a REALLY scenic route that sometimes involves making a full circle for something that was literally as easy as just turning left in the correct place.
•Point of interest search is slow and ineffective. Even with my ancient Garmin (and obviously with my phone), it would never find most places, even ones that have been there many years. This after waiting an interminable amount of time for the list to compile. Did I get the long update on my computer and add it to the GPS? Yep. I thought that was the problem, did the update, and then discovered it was Not the problem.
•Doesn’t appear to take traffic into account. Neither does my old Garmin, but it should do better than a piece of tech that’s 10 years old and at least be comparable to a current smartphone’s GPS; otherwise, what’s the point?
•Hard to stop. You want to sometimes say, “OK SHUT UP. I know the rest of the way!”, and in all other GPS systems I’ve tried, getting to the “end route/stop” place is usually two steps, max. It is long and complicated, and I don’t want to die in a car accident, so I end up having to suffer through unnecessary and often over-complicated routes that make no sense.
•Doesn’t default to turn-by-turn. Sometimes it shows an aerial view, which is zero helpful, has no detail, and requires me to think a lot about “is this to MY right or left if my car is facing this way and the map is oriented North Up and I *think* I am moving East maybe, but I can’t tell because this stupid thing is both dim and also has an unbelievably zoomed out map view where I’m not sure Where my little dot is going?!?!”

So yes. Unless I sit in the parking lot and fiddle with it for a good while, nothing is quite right, and everything takes a long time to find or set up. I tried it for a month now, and my opinion has not changed. This is frustrating.

Good things:
•nice size screen
•fun voices

Overall rating: 2 stars. I like Garmin more, and I am quite unhappy with this. It is slightly better than my now failing 10-year-old Garmin GPS. *slightly*. I would not buy this or recommend it. The interface is cumbersome, the visibility is bad in the sun, and finding places is a pain and basically 100% of the time requires me to just search for an address on my phone and plug it in. Nope.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions

text_fidelity_a:
Senso Bluetooth Headphones, Best Wireless Sports Earphones w/Mic IPX7 Waterproof HD Stereo Sweatproof Earbuds for Gym Running Workout 8 Hour Battery Noise Cancelling Headsets (Black Red) I have had way too many sets of headphones. Mostly because my dog eats them if they are within reach. While I still have not found the perfect headset with these, they come pretty close.

Durability and battery Life - Way too early to tell. I'll update this after a few months.

Noise Canceling- Let’s get something straight - if you put your fingers in your ears, they will cancel noise. That's called passive noise canceling, or simply, blocking outside noise. True active noise canceling head phones are over the ear, and usually very expensive. These head phones do a pretty good job passively blocking outside noise by fitting very well to the ear and being angled correctly.

Sound - Everyone has different tastes when it comes to what they like to hear. Some headphones have good or bad ranges from high to low. But it is the quality of the range that matters. For instance, I like to hear bass, and to me there is nothing worse than a tinny am radio sound. These definitely have bass, but it's a bit muddy. The good news is I was able to adjust the equalizer on my phone to clean it up, mostly. Overall all though, for the price, the sound quality is pretty darn good.

Fit & Hold - They Fit and stay put! The best part of these headphones is they fit my ears perfectly. The part that goes around the ear has a wire going through it, unlike so many others. This allows you to mold the over ear wires exactly to you ear and they do not fall out. None of the last several sets I had do this, and it is an enormous benefit.

Controls - The are typical up and down volume and a center button that is used for on, off, hold, answer, etc. I wish the volume buttons were reversed, but that's just being picky. They announce power on, power off and connected. Sadly, they do not announce battery life.

Appearance – Meh. They are a bit big and boxy, but I don’t know how that‘s different from having white things hanging out of your ears for $200.00

Overall - I am giving this 5 starts not because they are the best headphones. I am giving them 5 starts because they check off almost all of my boxes and the price it great. So, 5 stars for overall function and price.

Note: I paid full price for these and I was not asked to review them. Also, if you like this review, please indicate so below. Thanks.
text_fidelity_b: Senso Bluetooth Headphones, Best Wireless Sports Earphones w/Mic IPX7 Waterproof HD Stereo Sweatproof Earbuds for Gym Running Workout 8 Hour Battery Noise Cancelling Headsets (Black Red)

text_fidelity_a:
EarStudio ES100 MK2-24bit Portable High-Resolution Bluetooth Receiver/USB DAC/Headphone Amp with LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC (3.5mm Unbalanced & 2.5mm Balanced Output) Very nice features, sounds great, 2.5 balanced output! BT v5, aptXHD, top of the line DAC’s, great battery life. So why just 4 stars? The documentation leaves a lot to be desired. The included printed doc was about the size of a matchbook with writing so small it required a magnifying glass to read and for all that effort it basically said nothing. The biggest hassle was the pairing. It couldn’t be less intuitive. I have many BT devices, both receivers and transmitters and this is the first one that required a web search to figure out. Very frustrating. And to enable the BT v5 it requires a ROM flash upgrade so you have to connect it to a PC and follow a bunch of steps that are as intuitive as the pairing. I came within seconds of sending it back but stuck it out because it had some pretty stellar reviews. It turns out I’m glad I did. Once you get it sorted out it is a pretty amazing piece of kit. I use it with my HiBy r6 and BGVP DMG’S as well as my ATH M-50x headphones. I can now roam freely around the kitchen while keeping the DAP safely out of the way. I can plug-in the 2.5mm balanced cable and get outstanding sound with the added bonus of not heating up the DAP (it gets hot when plugged in directly) and the battery life of the HiBy is more than doubled. Both of these bonuses more than make up for the minor degradation in sound staging. I have listened for over 7 hours without the battery giving up, but have not used it up to it’s limit yet so I can’t say how long it will last. Is it worth the Benjamin it cost? Oh yeah.

Update: Upgraded to 5 stars after a month of use. Once the niggling little details were figured out and the unit was set up I can't say enough good things about this puppy. My main reason for getting a BT transmitter was I am going to be doing extensive bicycle touring later this year and since it will be solo touring I wanted good quality music available. I have an extensive library of 24 bit flac's as well as a couple of hundred audiobooks for the trip and while the playback of the books isn't important the music is. I invested a fair amount of cash into a HiBy R6 DAP and BGVP DMG IEM's as well as upgraded cables to connect them. The EarStudio lets me connect via 2.5" balanced with no real discernible degredation in the quality of the playback as opposed to plugging directly into the output on the DAP, and here's the kicker, instead of just getting 6 - 7 hours of playback and heating up the DAP I now get double that without any heat. I can stash the HiBy in a Pelican 1020 case and put it in my top tube bag where it's out of harms way and protected in case of misadventure. The EarStudio has a battery life of around 14 hours (I haven't run it out yet, and I have listened for over 8 hours). Added to that the App that is available for my Android based DAP is amazing. More fiddly bits than your above average geek could ever want. So I gotta give it a 5 star rating. And it's worth twicw the price but don't tell Radsone.
text_fidelity_b: EarStudio ES100 MK2-24bit Portable High-Resolution Bluetooth Receiver/USB DAC/Headphone Amp with LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC (3.5mm Unbalanced & 2.5mm Balanced Output)

text_fidelity_a:
PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black) I received these earphones from Amazon Vine in early January, 2018. I liked the over-the-ears design. It makes the earphones far less likely to fall off when exercising. The sound quality is also excellent. I found its wireless bluetooth function quite handy for listening to music on my smartphone while walking, biking, lifting weights or doing calisthenics.

In short, as long as the battery could be charged, these sport earphones worked quite well. But suddenly, a few weeks ago, after only 7 months of use, the battery simply would no longer take a charge. The manual says that the battery should last through up to 300 charges, and there is absolutely no way that in only seven months I charged this device 300 times. It holds a charge well while the battery is working, much better than the other bluetooth earbuds that I have owned. So I could use it for up to five days without charging the battery. This means that, in seven months, I only charged the battery about 42-50 times, at most. This means the life of the battery was a mere 16% of what the manufacturer promised!

This is not a device in which the battery can be replaced. Therefore, once the battery dies, the earphones are worthless. Since the warranty is only for 90 days, there is no recourse with the manufacturer for replacing this device after that length of time.

The way that this product works is a good idea, but until the design includes the possibility of replacing the battery, the high price is simply not worth it. I will have to stick to cheap earbuds which are not such a hit to my pocketbook when their non-replaceable battery dies.

I rate this product as follows:

Sound quality 5 stars
Durability of battery: 1 star
Value for price: 1 star
Overall average: 2.3 stars

text_fidelity_a:
Sony RX100 IV 20.1 MP Premium Compact Digital Camera w/ 1-inch Sensor, 4K Movies and 40x Super Slow Motion HD DSCRX100M4/B Black I've said it a thousand times: "I think I could really get into (real) photography, but I just can't take another hobby that requires me carrying a whole bag of equipment across the world. If I get a DSLR, I won't take it to the places that I'd like to use it the most." Well...I think they made this camera just for me. I believe this camera to be capable of "real" pro photos, just the same as if I bought a DSLR and a single lens, which many people start by doing. It also makes a startup punk like me look like a pro, much to the chagrin of the real pros.

My other cameras include a DSC-H20, which is an older Sony model with a 10x zoom lens, multiple point-and-shoots, and a waterproof/shockproof Panasonic that I really like for my basic, worry-free shots.

My main question about this camera was, why does it appear to be Sony's flagship compact camera in every way, but yet it doesn't have the 30x optical zoom lens that some of the other Sony's have (or even the 10x of my DSC-H20)? I knew there would be an answer, but to find it, I had to start digging into camera specs, something I've been meaning to do for a while.

First, pro photographers tend to think that if you're using much zoom under most circumstances, then you're just being lazy. You need to get closer. In a landscape shot, zoom tends to flatten things out. I may have never noticed this, or WHY this is. You know, you go on vacation, take a lot of pictures, come back and some look great and others look bad. Maybe it's true that every time I zoom in on a landscape, I'm really just ruining my shot.

The other thing is aperture. Aperture basically tells you how clear the background of your picture will be versus your foreground (I'm just learning this myself, so camera pros, feel free to comment with better verbiage), a lower number being better if you want a totally clear picture, and the lowness of that number being what you use to compare the quality of lenses. It's also good to have a high end on the range because that allows you to take those artsy photos with something super clean up front and a blurry background. I've also seen some neat head shots taken that way, where even some hair starts becoming blurry.

Anyway, the low aperture on this camera is 1.8 all the way zoomed out, and 2.8 all the way zoomed in (you can set it as high as 11 in either case). This is a tight range with great numbers (notice that even here, you lose a little bit by using zoom). My camera with the 10x zoom has an aperture equal to 3.5 all the way out, similar to the 30x zoom cameras Sony has now. It makes a big difference, even to my amateur eye.

This camera, and my subsequent research, has allowed me to let go of the 10/30x zoom. Yes, those cameras are great, but this is the flagship mini for a reason. Now I understand. Just taking random pictures in my neighborhood, although so boring compared to my favorite International backgrounds, I can clearly see a quality difference.

The other main spec for cameras is shutter speed. This can be set for 1/32000 of a second all the way up to 30 seconds. The quickest shutter speeds will capture an instant in time without blur, while the slower ones will capture more action with some blur. They are also good for low light scenarios to expose the shot to more light. Very slow speeds should be used with a tripod or the camera set down someplace. This camera makes a noise (not an obnoxious one) when on auto and using a slower shutter speed, to keep you still. It's very intuitive and works well.

While you will get better shots than you ever had before using this camera on auto, the dial wheel allows you to set either aperture or shutter speed as a priority and leave the rest on auto, perfect for people that want to understand what a real camera can do, and who want to set up pro shots without yet knowing everything.

The controls on this thing are awesome. I love that there is no touchscreen to fight with and that everything is so intuitive. Great praise to Sony for knowing what fads aren't worth it. (One fad they did latch onto is that 180 degree rotating screen, which really is fantastically convenient and feels quite strong and well done). While we're talking about it, they also put in the fantastic viewfinder and the pop-up flash, which all completely recess into the body of this thing (an amazing work of engineering art).

Speaking of the flash, you won't use it often. Even on a cheap camera, I try to keep the flash off, but this thing does an amazing job of using ambient light for exposure (I believe this is the third pillar of photography). I swear, I have never seen such clear pictures in very low light. Instead of being grainy, I can pick up minute details (even zoom-able), and they appear brighter than the actual place they were taken. This, I believe, is because of the 1" image sensor they are touting. I'm impressed.

The 960fps thing. With only two seconds, this may be hard to set up the shot you want, but 2 seconds seems a lot longer in 960fps. Even just shaking your leg on camera, you'll see the odd aftereffects of your socks moving like you never did before. Stupid example, but that's the point: the details you get from 960fps slow-mo are amazing.

4k video. I really didn't care about all this until some guy at a conference pointed out how 4k has been used for pro video for years. Instead of multiple cameras to cover a hockey game, for example, you could just use one and zoom in on anything you want and still have high-def video. I realized we probably will move over to actually using it at some point. Well, here's your chance to actually use that 4k TV. It's awesome. It really is.

A note on SD cards. While most devices can read SDHC cards, which went up to 32GB, the reason they want you to have a SDXC card (which can be from 64GB to 2TB in theory) is because the speed ratings are higher. You need the speed rating of 3 (>100 Mbps) to really use these big data transfer functions. I suspect the 960fps is all that can be held in RAM, and that those speeds are way too fast for even the newest and best card (hence the 2 second limit on 960fps).

Suffice to say that I love this camera. I appreciate each of its mechanical and electrical features and how they're perfectly integrated to make this small, marvelous camera. Even in the leather case (not included), it's about the same size as my H20, certainly portable enough to have it when you want it, but with enough features and technology that you're not sacrificing anything in your photography.
text_fidelity_b: Sony RX100 IV 20.1 MP Premium Compact Digital Camera w/ 1-inch Sensor, 4K Movies and 40x Super Slow Motion HD DSCRX100M4/B Black

Recently, I ordered a pack of the blue and black version of this film. I was surprised at how much I had missed the process of trying to frame a shot, pulling the trigger, and waiting to see what I was going to get. The phone cameras are so good and so easy that I do not even carry a point-and-shoot anymore. But there is no guesswork with them. You get an immediate do-over, and you can fix what you don't like.

This is more interesting and more fun. At least, to me.

The film itself is very close to the original. I did not have any camera jams, but I remember having them. This film is expensive per shot, so those jams will be annoying if/when they do occur, but I plan to keep ordering and shooting this.

Bose SoundTrue around-ear wired headphones II - Apple devices, Navy Blue When I shop for headphones, I shop primarily for comfort. I’m not a sound snob -- I just need headphones that are super comfortable.

My last was a pair of Skullcandy’s, Hesh style, and I couldn’t wear them for more than 2-3 hours. These Bose SoundTrue’s feel a little lighter, and the ear cups are oval, not round, which makes them fit me better. They also don’t feel as tight on my head as the Skullcandy’s, but I don’t feel like they’re going to fall off.

Soundwise, I think they’re fine. But as I said, I’m not a sound snob, so as long as music sounds good and not like it’s played through a tin can, I’m happy.

Convenience wise, the ear cups swivel so the headphones fit in the included flat case. They don’t fold up a lot, but the case will be handy for when I want to take the headphones out with me. The cord is detachable, and has a remote for music/phone call control. I received the Apple version to review, so only the play/pause worked on my phone, but the other functions worked on my Macbook Air.

text_fidelity_a:
iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice There are both positives and negatives about this product, my perspective being that I am using it to replace an old-sko0l red LED alarm buzzer with staticy radio.

+ Looks sleeker (one would hope, as the old had a plastic wood finish), smaller footprint, and slightly raised clock makes it easier to see.

+ I love the USB port, so I can get rid of two power cords and replace it with one.

+ Shows the weather as according to Accuweather, which is at least a rough estimate of what it's like outside.

+ Better sound if you want to set it to stream music.

+ Shows the date.

+ 2 programmable buttons allow you to control "smart" devices. This could be really handy if you have a light for the room plugged into a receptacle across the room. You could also cut your overhead light cord and put in a socket for control from your bed if you're into that sort of thing. I just have a lamp beside the bed, so I really don't care, but this is something I can actually see being useful.

+ Can use it as a Bluetooth speaker. Would be better if you could integrate it with other home WiFi speakers, even though I'm more into big, hardwired speakers for serious listening from a whole-house audio system

Things that are both positive and negative, so I guess I have to call them neutral:

= microphone has a button to turn it off. A switch would be more believable, and then it wouldn't have a red light showing on the top all the time. I have no doubts the CIA can still turn it on, but I like to think the manufacturer won't listen in. I'm sure they could have put a back door in, too, but I would hope they would be sued severely if that is ever discovered. The red light is good when talking on the phone to show the phone is muted but otherwise the light shouldn't be on all the time...

= Buttons on the top are always lit up, which I consider to be a negative. Should be able to control them separately. Front display has 6 dim levels and off, and the lowest level is good for sleeping even with the thing pointed at you (at least in my opinion), but then it's really not bright enough during the day (at least if it's a bright day). I know it's petty, but I'm really not into doing anything more than I already do to get ready for bed, and that includes pressing a button 5 or 6 times to get it back to the way I wanted it. Should work on a light sensor or just be able to program it for day and evening. I mention this stuff because I'm sure it can be added via firmware (not the sensor part, obviously). Overall, not as bright as the old red LED thing, but somehow less see-able.

= You can do random light shows with the colored LEDs at the bottom. I suppose setting it to come on before your alarm is useful, but just playing with them is not.

Negatives:

- I just hate the Internet sometimes, and this reminds me why. (I'm a fairly young Systems Engineer, FYI, so it's not that I'm some geezer that can't use technology). I just hate that I need an app to control this thing. It's an alarm clock, so shouldn't I be able to do the basics without my phone? Is this just so they can get on my phone and steal my data/identity/whatever? I got news for you guys - I set this kind of crap up with a burner phone that is linked to fake Email, fake everything, location and everything else turned off. Let me at least set the bloody time without hooking up to the Internet! What happens when Comcast freezes and my WiFi temporarily doesn't have Internet connection?

To use Spotify with this (which I don't use and never will since I just have all the music I could ever want on a local server), you have to buy the Premium version. I'm sure that was absolutely necessary. Is anything not contrived multi-layered big business anymore?

Just to DL the app, Google and my burner phone both try to trick me into thinking I have to put credit card details in to get it. Sometimes I'm just ready to forego the digital age and find an old ticking clock that loses 5 minutes every day to run my life by. I am so sick and tired of adds, apps that want to control and steal your life, and companies that can't think further than next quarter...

- No battery backup. Should be built in. Even my '70s POS could be backed up via 9v battery. It saves some settings, but turns back to archaic Fahrenheit on me when power is lost...

- ...worse...when power comes back on, it screams at you. Power in my area is good, but on occasion goes out for a few seconds multiple times in a night. That may be the end of this thing (OK, I just lowered my star rating to 3, because the truth is, that probably will be the end of this thing's reign in my bedroom).

- No radio. No internal memory for music. You're at the mercy of streaming accounts and everything working properly on your network.

- Going along with the first negative point, you can't even set an alarm with this thing if you don't sign in with an Amazon account and do the Alexa thing. More ways to get grips on you. More ways to complicate a simple alarm clock.

Do I really hate simple and easy so much? I almost gave this four stars due to the fact that it looks pretty and adds some functionality, but what's wrong with a highly visible dump clock beside the bed? That's all I'm using this for, when it all comes down to it. Well, my feelings may change for the better when they inevitably fix some of the simple things on this that they can do by firmware. I will let you know if my feelings change significantly.
text_fidelity_b: iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice

text_fidelity_a:
Sony 16GB Microvault USB Flash Drive for Smartphone (USM16SA1/B) After reading the comments here, I decided to not bother with the Sony software. I installed "Nexus Media Importer" from the Google Android app store and it automatically detects and mounts the Sony device. I can read and write files with no problem, including playing audio and video files without copying them to the phone memory. On my PC, the Sony device mounts like any other flash drive. I would give this 5 stars if it was $30 (and if it came with better instructions), but the $45 price seems high for what is essentially a flash drive with a micro-USB port. You can get the same functionality (in a larger form factor) by using a regular flash drive and an OTG cable (sold here on Amazon for less than $2).

EDIT: I'm still happy with this device, but since writing this review, I've noticed that several other companies (SanDisk and others) have come out with similar products (flash drives with both micro and regular USB connectors) and some of them have much faster USB3.0 speeds. Sony has reduced their price to be competitive. Shop around; I expect functionality is similar.

text_fidelity_a: SABRE Wireless Window Glass Vibration Alarm With High and Low Sensitivity Settings, 115dB, Audible Up To 700-Feet (213-Meters), Includes SABRE Home Security Decal, Battery Test Button This pair of door window alarms is affordable but performance wise, uneven. Application is easy. They stick on without issue. Battery operated they come with two setting, high and low. the batteries are included and there is also a low battery detector which insures your alarms are operational. A large red decal provides potential intruders with an obvious warning. that being said, the alarm performance is not consistent. Power Strip with 3 USB, KPSTEK Flat Plug Extension Cord with 2 Widely Spaced Outlets, Desktop Charging Station for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, Black - KS2312 This is a combination product with a 5 foot extension cord, 2 AC power outlets, and 3 full-sized USB power ports. Compact size is great for travel, since older hotels don't have enough power outlets for modern travelers and the outlets are often hidden behind desks or under beds.

Unfortunately, the USB power ports are pretty weak. You get 2.4A divided among 3 ports, so if you're trying to charge 3 devices, each one gets less than 1A. Modern smartphones and tablets will often fast-charge at 3A, so charging with these ports will be very slow. USB powered laptops can use even more power and will complain about being charged at less than 3A.

I don't like that there is no USB-C charging port and no USB Power Delivery fast charging, which are becoming the standard for smartphones and laptops.

This device is not UL listed for electrical safety. As phone and tablet and laptop batteries get more and more powerful, electrical safety becomes more and more important. Most power strips from US brands are UL listed, so I cannot recommend a product that is not UL listed.

Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector Although this is a very compact speaker (roughly 4.5 inches long and a little over 2 inches tall) it puts out a surprisingly decent sound - better than I expected given the price point. The treble and mid range were pretty clear, and the bass, while a bit light (unavoidable given the compact size) is more than adequate for casual listening.

Usage is very straightforward. I had zero problems pairing this with a Fire 8.9 tablet and a Nexus 7. The Bluetooth range is excellent - no dropouts even with the tablet on the far side of the room (a good 30 feet from the speaker). It also has the ability to direct connect to the sound source via a standard RCA cable.

The build quality seems solid, with nicely finished seams on the plastic case. The controls on the back (on/off, charge input and RCA in) and are clearly marked. The volume, pause, etc. controls are on the top and are very nicely done - they light up with a red light when touched. Very clear, easy to use, and attractive to boot.

It also comes with a decent carry pouch, which will come in handy to protect it from scratches when carried in a backpack. The "manual" is sparse, but is not really needed -- very easy to figure out how to use this. It comes in a sturdy box, which is good for not only storing it, but also to help prevent shipping damage. (Alas, there are also some unfortunate spelling errors on the product info printed on the box.)

My main complaint, and the reason for a loss of one star, is that it has an internal, non-removable battery. Eventually the battery will fail (e.g., not be able to retain a charge) rending the speaker useless (or requiring a constant tethering to a power source). While non-removable batteries allow for a more compact size, I'd be more than happy to trade some size for the ability to replace the battery.

That one issue aside, this is a very nice speaker for the price.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector

Wyze Cam Outdoor Starter Bundle (Base Station and 1 Cam), 1080p HD Indoor/Outdoor Wire-Free Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, White with Camo Skin Originally, I had a Wyze camera and decided to use it outdoor to watch a duck that nested outside of our front door. Once I got the outdoor covers though, I realized I couldn't make it work. I then bought these 2 outdoor cameras and I am so glad I did. The price and the quality are unbeatable. We have a Ring for our front door. It is good but I think it would not work well for what we are using the cameras for. We have one camera outside hidden monitoring the duck and one put up on the ceiling of our lanai to monitor our pool area where our cat hangs out. She has fallen in the pool several times and we worry about her not being able to get out as she gets older. This camera is amazing. The picture is awesome. The sound would be perfect if we didn't receive some random signal from something else electronic around us. It is as if someone has the same frequency for a radio. However, we really don't need it to have sound or to be able to talk to someone. We want to watch our cat and see when she is at the back door ready to come inside. The one watching the duck has no issues with sound or microphone. The duck actually looks at the camera when you talk to her! :-) We use the share options to let our family watch the duck too! We will use the "duck" cam somewhere else once she has moved on. Very happy I went with these two cameras.

In addition, I didn't use the screws to install either camera. The "duck" cam will be moved eventually and needed to be on the soffit of our house. I obviously do not want holes in the soffit especially when it is not a permanent camera spot. I used an outdoor, double-stick tape by 3M to put it in place. I did this also with the camera for our pool as I didn't want to use screws in the lanai cover. The tape is holding perfectly and the lanai cam will probably stay there with the tape.

The "duck" cam is viewed a lot throughout the day so I would say the battery runs down quickly. The lanai cam is viewed less and I have only a few motion detection settings set up so the battery went down to 17% in a little less than one month. Easy to pop the cam off and charge quickly and then replace it.
text_fidelity_b: Wyze Cam Outdoor Starter Bundle (Base Station and 1 Cam), 1080p HD Indoor/Outdoor Wire-Free Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, White with Camo Skin

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black This is my first purchase of earbuds in the over $200 category. I got the Jabra Elite 65t as soon as they came out and have since bought a couple of other pairs of earbuds in the under $100 category that had better features like IPX7 or 8hr battery life. Therefore I was excited to upgrade to the XM4 for their bettery life and the noise canceling.

Unfortunately, I've had several issues with these. I don't have particularly small ears. Usually the medium tips fit without issue. On the XM4, I started with the medium tips and tested their air tightness using the app. The small tips don't have any kind of seal on my ears without really shoving them super far down my ear canal, so I decided to stick with the medium size. Unfortunately, I have experienced significant ear fatigue enough so that I can't wear the earbuds for more than a couple of hours. I have since switched to the small tips for the sake of comfort, but that means sacrificing any passive noise canceling - and unless I have a defective unit, without the passive noise canceling in addition to the active noise canceling, there is absolutely no difference between having the noise canceling on and off. To me, this completely defeats the purpose of buying noise canceling earbuds.

I also have had issues with connectivity such as the bluetooth connection on my phone suddenly dropping and having to go into the app to manually pair them again.

In terms of battery life, depending on the control settings of each earbud, there can be a difference in the drain of battery between the left and right side. On a bad day, I had a 30% difference with the right draining significantly faster. My earbuds are using the factory settings with the playback controls on the right and the noise canceling on the left for reference.

Both the connectivity problems and the bettery difference between the earbuds has seemed to have gotten better since performing a factory reset, but be aware that there is still a little difference in the rate of battery drain between the L and R earbuds (It's not super significant now and maybe reaches under 7-8% difference at the end of the day).

I bought some Comply foam tips, which I hope will fix the discomfort issue and make the noise canceling work at the optimal rate without the ear fatigue. However, I shouldn't have to modify almost $300 earbuds to make them work like they should. It would help if Sony would offer more sizes of ear tips to help make them more usable for a wider population. Then again, if I have gripes like these, then maybe the XM4s aren't for me. Makes me super sad considering I think that they're probably fantastic for most people.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black

Start-up was fast, almost super fast. You open the cover and BAM, within seconds, you're online. Very cool.

The display is HD and very crisp. I viewed a couple of Netflix nature movies and the display was stunning. No lag or fuzziness. There's a Micro HDMI so you can view on a big screen, but a cable is not included.

The wi-fi is dual-band 802.11 and is fast as well. I had no issues connecting at home, work, or the local coffee shop.

There is 16gb of local storage, but Google includes 100gb of Google Drive storage for 2 years. Personally I've never used more than 3gb of storage, so 100gb should be adequate for most people.

The internal speakers weren't great, but they didn't suck either. Sound was crisp but slightly muted. A pair of USB speakers took care of this. Soon I was rocking in the coffee shop (i forgot my headphones).

Because of my big fingers I'm not a fan of the pad thingy. I was able to plug in a bluetooth mouse and was up and running within 30 seconds. At first I wasn't sure if the Chromebook would allow peripherals, but it did with no issues.

The battery is stated to last 13 hours. I haven't gone that far yet, but I've gotten a solid 5 hours of mixed internet/video streaming use and still had 50% battery left.

The fit and finish is top notch although the top cover can be a finger print magnet. I just throw a microfiber cloth in my bag.

The keyboard has ample sized 'chicklet' keys which are soft and silent. My big fingers had no issues hitting other keys by accident.

In closing, I'm a convert!

My laptops were mainly used for the internet and watching movies. With everything online, like Netflix, Hulu, and Prime movies, this Chromebook rocks!
text_fidelity_b: ASUS C201PA-DS02 11.6-Inch Laptop (Navy Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz S1 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones With Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod Update: Changing tips really improved these phones. The tri flange tips really hit the sweet spot in my ear. I can 'tune' the bass now by how far I shove them in my ears.

Still not for critical listening but a very easy to listen to headphone. Cymbals sound better now. Bass is more balanced with good extension/bloom for < $100 IEM's. They are forgiving of poor source material and/or using with portable electronics. They strike a good middle ground between musical and detailed, though it's somewhat a case of not doing either one particularly well but that's getting nit picky.

The phones are bit bulky and heavy and the cord bounces while running. I also find I tend to futz with them a lot while wearing them. Adjusting the fit, playing with the cables, etc. But all and all they fit well and stay put for most activities. The thicker/flat cord bothers me at times. It always feels like it's going to come off my ears but in reality it doesn't. I think with more wearing they will drape nicer over the ear.

But to my ear they still lack 'something'. If I had to do it over I'd probably try the NuForce 700's or Thinksound ts02/MS01.

Upping my rating to 4 stars for being perfectly good, if some what uninspiring phones.

Original review:
Too thumpy and not in a good way. It's all, ok mostly boom with no 'good' thud. (I'm guesing there are even boomier headphones I out there.

I got them an hour a go and I already know they are going back.

And I like bass and I like warm and forgiving over 'accurate' and 'lively'.

I like the $22 Vsonic GR99 better than these. Though to be fair these are 'technically' and are better in the treble than both of them but it's not enough to offset the excessive bass for me and again I like bass. If you want to hear not just the bass drum but also the beater side of the bass drum these are not the phones for you. If you like the sound of all the drums, including the rack toms, these are not for you.

If you want to hear bass instruments that sound like they do in real life, these are not for you.

They are so V-shaped they sound like they have hole in the frequency response. If you know what that means and feel like you hear that kind of things these are not the phones for you, if like me you are being swayed by the number of good reviews.

If you think 'beats' sound good you might like these. If you 'bump' in the car and or like hip hop/rap than you might like these. If you are coming from crap phones you might like these because they probably have better highs and more bass extension (rumble I see people call it and rumble it is, and not in a good bass extension way). If your frame of reference for drum sounds is EDM you may very well like these.

I'll be returning these and sticking with the GR99 until I can find something better. I don't think these are worth the $60 they cost based on owning Vsonic VC02 and Vsonic VSD1's (which I really liked but just couldn't get a good fit).

While the highs have fairly nice extension and no sibilance or tizzinesss don't expect to hear the metal of the cymbals, mostly you get the sound of the tip of the drum stick on the cymbals. But that is pretty common until you get to better phones/speakers. While not expensive the Vsonic VC02 was very good at 'cymbal' sounds.

These are v-shapped to the point of sounding like they have hole in the frequency response. If you know what that means and think you can hear such a thing, these phone are definitely not for you, in case like me you are being swayed by the number of good reviews.

Do they sound 'terrible' no, unless you have heard better. Do not get these if you are looking for good phones with a little more bass than what you have now I like I was trying to do over the Vsonic VC02. I like the VC02 but wanted something with more bass to use while working out. I also like my Vsonic VSD1's but I put them through the wash and never could get a very good fit, so I'm not replacing them.

I was worried about these and the bass sound but wanted to try them since I almost always wear phones with the cord over my ears. and in that aspect they are pretty comfortable and were easy to fit and get a good seal with the stock size tips. They feel a little big to me but I'm coming from Vsonic VC02 which are very small.

All music was 320k MP3 or FLAC using the DAC headphone amp in the Topping VX1 amp using foobar 2000.

If accurate reproduction of bass sounds, including drum sounds is important to you look else where.

I like BASS. The GR99 are bass heavy as are the Skull Titans. The Vsonic VSD1 are not shy of bass compared to other phones, but the bass sounds more natural on those even though they are bass heavy in comparison to accurate/neutral phones.

I'm being generous giving them 3 stars but 2 stars felt too low since so many people like them and mine is just one opinion. One persons and one person's boomy is another person's good bass extension.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz S1 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones With Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod

Belkin N300 Wireless N Router (Latest Generation) (F9K1002) Bought this for my mother who has a small 2 bedroom apartment. Has been installed for over 3 weeks now. It was so very easy to install, simple instructions, did not have to adjust any settings. We just attached it to the DSL modem, loaded the CD into each computer that was going to use the network, followed the simple instructions, works great. We did have a problem trying to set up an account, which we still have not been able to do. May call later for assistance if we find it would be helpful to have an account, but so far everything works great.

We have had my mother's desktop computer (also running wireless now), her notebook computer, my notebook computer and the printer all running on the network at the same time. There was absolutely no degradation in service, have never had a problem with disconnects even with all computers running at the same time and two of the computers sending documents to the printer. This includes using one of the notebook computers at the furthest location in the apartment away from the router as possible. The only problem we have is the slower Verizon DSL service compared to the faster Verizon FIOS service I have at my house, so not a Belkin problem. Too bad my mother can't get FIOS. But her internet access is as fast as it was when it was attached directly to the modem.

Would highly recommend this product.

5/28/2015 - Just found this review I wrote in 2011. My mother is still using the same Belkin N150, still works great even if we have 3 computers running at the same time. The retirement community she lives in switched voice/Internet carriers about 6 months ago. Saw no difference in performance. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin N300 Wireless N Router (Latest Generation) (F9K1002)

ASUS VS197D-P 18.5" WXGA 1366x768 VGA Back-lit LED Monitor, Black I'm very pleased with this monitor. I needed to replace my second screen and didn't want to spend a lot, but needed a monitor with 1920x1200 resolution. This seemed like a decent bet. It has exceeded my expectations with regard to performance. The clarity is excellent -- it rivals my primary screen which cost three times as much!

The monitor is very lightweight. It comes with both DVI and VGA cables, which was unexpected. I like that there's no power transformer or wall wart. It has just a regular power cord. Set up is simple (just attached the base and no tools are needed).

Of course, at this price point some features are not present. For example, while the screen can be tilted back and forth a bit, it does not have any up/down adjustment, nor can it be swiveled into portrait mode. There's no USB connectors and no speakers. But for me, none of those were deal breakers. I wanted a good quality monitor that was affordable, and this hit the mark 100%. Plus, it does not scrimp on connections. There's DVI, VGA and HDMI. I'm using DVI at present since the PC I'm using it with is a few years old. But, my next PC will probably have a HDMI connection, making this monitor future-proof (well, as future-proof as any tech product can be).

If you're looking for a basic monitor that does not scrimp on image quality, this should definitely be on your short list. Also, check Amazon Warehouse for used ones. I got mine there (it was probably a customer's return). It looks brand new, and only ran me $127.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS VS197D-P 18.5" WXGA 1366x768 VGA Back-lit LED Monitor, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle, 6" E Ink Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I'm a big fan of Kindle e-Readers. We own two of the older generation ones (the last Kindles with keyboard) and for x-mas I bought my mother a Kindle Fire HD 8.9 for x-mas. But, alas, she doesn't seem to have fine enough motor control to hit the small buttons on that device (see my review for that device). So the Fire has been sitting unused on the coffee table for a few months now.

But this is not a review of the Fire HD 8.9. I want to describe my very short experience with the basic Kindle and the Kindle Paperwhite - as they relate to the intended user: my mom. She recently suffered a stroke and one of the side effects is that she now has a constant tremble in her left hand. As she had trouble with the Fire HD 8.9 we went to Staples to see if the more purpose-built Kindles were easier to operate. We were not surprised when she often made mistakes selecting books on the Paperwhite's touch screen. But we were surprised to find that she couldn't even handle the physical buttons on the basic Kindle! From what I could tell, the problems were: the side-buttons (page forward/backward) are much smaller and narrower than they were on our old Kindles (which my mom had no trouble with), so basic navigation among pages became iffy. Similarly, the D-pad is smaller too - and that made selection of books difficult for her. Finally, while I could easily hold my old Kindle with one hand AND operate the page forward button, this is a bit more difficult with the new basic Kindle. My mom could not manage it at all. And since she can't hold the Kindle with her trembling left hand, neither e-Reader was for her. [She is now making do with the Kindle Fire HD 8.9 by laying it on a flat surface and only operating it with her right hand].

I'm still giving the Kindle 4 stars because none of these shortcomings are of interest to the majority of people, but I wanted folks to be aware of the newer devices' potential limitations with those suffering from limited motor skills.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle, 6" E Ink Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Philips MANT940 UHF Digital and Analog Indoor/Outdoor Antenna (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I'm within ten miles of 13 transmitters, but on the far slope (for most) of a densely-wooded hill. I used to get pretty good reception from an old aluminum christmas-tree type attic-mounted (non-amplified) antenna, but broke it accidentally. This amplified MANT940 is just as good, and a WHOLE lot smaller and easier to manipulate!

Attached to my Philips 5603D, this device (and 25 feet of extension cable) is providing me with 31 digital channels!?! Not always perfectly clearly (that is, there's occasional smear and freezing), but it's attached to an outside wall next to a window and easy to tweak - there's probably a better position, but this is convenient. So far I'm also getting 11 analog channels, but they're all dups. Some of the digital ones are pure advertising, and not all are HDTV, but WHOA - CBS! UNbelievable high def picture, and GREAT signal (WHYY sucks.) Beat THIS price, Comcast/FiOS!

BTW, I can now say most channels give great signal - even in a snowstorm!!!
text_fidelity_b: Philips MANT940 UHF Digital and Analog Indoor/Outdoor Antenna (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Bose QuietComfort 35 II Wireless Bluetooth Headphones, Noise-Cancelling, with Alexa Voice Control - Black Back when I used to spend my days fumbling with earbud wires, I wondered "What kind of idiot would pay $300 dollars for headphones, when you can hear your sounds perfectly fine for less than $10?". Even as these products rose more and more to popularity, I scoffed and resisted.

Those days are long gone. After I borrowed them from my friend for a day and tried them myself, I knew why. After getting them, these quickly became a non-negotiable part of my life. I use them to:

- take and receive meetings
- freely go pee, refill coffee, and wash my dishes while listening to a meeting
- go on runs while listening to music
- ignore noisy people around me
- get myself into a state of focus
- calm my anxiety on airplanes
- show people I am not interested to talk to them
- as a fashion statement

Seriously, I wear these so much I think I am developing a bald spot. Maybe that's why all the engineers are bald. The sound quality is superb, and so is the bluetooth range and connectivity. I have since tried the Sony's, Dolby dimensions, the newer model of these, but these are the best one. I have bought a pair for my whole family, and replaced my old pair when it got old without a second thought. One time, I tried my friend's airpods and almost threw up at the sound quality. Not to mention, with this size, they are much harder to lose.

These are my favorite product of the last several years (this, and the divacup) and I would wholeheartedly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Bose QuietComfort 35 II Wireless Bluetooth Headphones, Noise-Cancelling, with Alexa Voice Control - Black

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White This product is a winner. The echo.system is here to stay. I was around during the early days of Internet technology working in the field. I had a knack for knowing what was going to be part of our future of technology and what was not. I still have that knack. This is an amazing product. I bought 2 of them. 1 for the living room. 1 for the bedroom. Every day they work on it from their end to give it more and more functionality meaning more things that it can do. You can pretty much hook it up to any Bluetooth speaker if you decide that you want better sound for music. I purchased speakers for each unit that were not related to Amazon in any way, just because I needed specialty products. I just have the unit you see here and not the ones with the more advanced speakers and so I cannot speak to them. But of the many many abilities it has, the ability to pull up music, TV, movies and more, some of my favorite things are the simplest. Instant forecasts anywhere in the world, timers and an alarm that you activate merely by speaking to it has really helped me in many ways. Do you want to know the time? Ask Alexa. Do you want to know today's forecast or next week's forecast? Just ask. They are meant to be on 24 hours a day and are activated by voice and so there are no lights on to bother a person when they are sleeping. I put the one in the bedroom not just to operate the television, but more of an alarm clock thing. So if I need to take a nap before my next client, wake me up in one hour. It's that easy. Lying in bed at night and asking what time it is or saying: wake me up at 7 AM. Done. I do not believe this product will replace computers remote controls nor telephones, but I think that it will be a wonderful companion to it, infinite information availability, and who knows what's coming in the future. The upgrades are done on their end so you do not have to buy new units as they upgrade. How cool is that? So far both of these units have worked flawlessly and I have had them for about a month now. Completely unobtrusive, and with plug-in units that are available, you can even run your household lights, appliances and more. I purchased a few of these things and they work perfectly. All my guests who have seen how this operates have been astounded and now they all want one. You can't beat the price. Now I am not hooked into Amazon in any way. I just love good solid technology that is the wave of the future. I cannot speak highly enough of these products. I am a very technological person and I have very high expectations for my technology that I purchase and this particular unit that I am reviewing is the one that I have. It works perfectly and I just love it.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

But this FiiO is like the candle you burn from both ends, you know, twice the light but half the time. This thing will drive ANY IEM’s you have to ear bleeding levels and when you look you’re at 45, OUT OF 100 on the volume scale. And while I am an IEM guy I do own a pair of HiFiMan HE-400i planars and I rarely see anything above 55 on the volume with it on Hi Gain. And granted they are only 35 ohm I have it on good authority that they will drive the big boys with out breaking a sweat. The only gripe I have is the battery life. I only run 2.5mm balanced so the battery usually taps out after about 5-6 hours. Not bad, but not the ES100’s 10 hours. But the power, man this sucker punches way above it’s weight. I use it mainly with my Samsung Galaxy phone and strictly LDAP. Everything else is disabled in the software/app that FiiO provides. And that is my second gripe. The ES100 rules on the app side. If FiiO put some time and money into providing similar functionality into their red headed stepchild app they could ask twice the price and I’d still think it was a bargain. But all the gripes aside it is definitely a step up from the ES100. Some told me if you have the Radsone that you’re good to go, no need to buy the FiiO. Fiddlesticks, BahHumbug and all those other quaking aphorisms. Buy it. It will make you smile.
text_fidelity_b: FiiO BTR5-384K/32Bit Native DSD256 Hi-Res CSR8675 Bluetooth5.0 Receiver/USB DAC/DSD Headphone Amp with LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC (3.5mm Unbalanced&2.5mm Balanced Output, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMP-BDT230 Smart Wi-Fi 3D Blu-Ray Player (2013 Model) The good:

Streaming is awesome. It doesn't hiccup or give any trouble, not even with the new Super HD format from Netflix. It has the normal selection, Hulu, Amazon, Netflix, Vudu, and they all work trouble free.

It has an Ethernet port and built-in WiFi, so you can connect to the Internet however works for you.

Setup is fast and easy. It's light weight and has about as small a footprint as I've seen on such a device. Definitely good for those tight on space in their entertainment center.

The bad:

The player is slow. It takes me an average of 30 seconds to a minute from the time I press the power button to the time I can watch the disk that's already in the drive.

The UI is clunky and hard to get used to. Things just don't do what standard UI design suggests they should do. You'll get used to it in time, but it's an unnecessary learning curve.

The UI allows for customization, but it is meaningless. You can't have one person's Hulu account tied to their profile, and a second person's Hulu account tied to their profile. It's just main menu color schemes and the line.

Overall, it's a solid player, and it does everything it needs to do. If you like the features, they are exactly as described. Just be aware of the delay in launching any disks or streaming sources.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMP-BDT230 Smart Wi-Fi 3D Blu-Ray Player (2013 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
TP-LINK TL-PA511 KIT AV500 Powerline Gigabit Adapter Starter Kit, up to 500Mbps I wish I would have tried these a long time ago. Could have saved me a lot of aggravation over the years. I'm sure a lot of people have heard of these and are likely sceptical. At least that's my excuse. That and I live in an old house with old wiring and many circuits. It's a San Francisco Victorian with bent hallways and a nightmare for both cell reception and WiFi range.

I have wanted to get networking from the back of the flat to the front. That seemingly simple concept never works. What I did get to work was to put WiFi in the back, and then a WiFi extender in the front with a 20' antenna extension which then pushed the antenna to the middle. Even that was tricky.

I even once tried a Verizon 4G LTE router to get some broadband in the front. It was expensive and still didn't work. So I pretty much resigned myself to just running cat5e or cat6 cable down the hallway, which is what I wanted to avoid. But right before I did that I decided to give this a shot.

The install took all of 5 seconds, seriously. Plug a box into one outlet in the back of the flat. Plug that box into my switch. Now run to the front of the flat. Plug that box into an outlet. Run the Ethernet from that box to my switch. Plug Linux box into switch. Boot up and test the speed. 53 MB/sec down, 4 up. Pretty much my ISP limit. My only concern is security, but they do have software, but it requires Windows I bet. I use Linux. I'll see what I can do to lock this down. But it does work. Fantastically so. Not sure the front and back are on the same circuit. Guessing they are. Either way, I finally got the front connected to the back without WiFi or a long Ethernet running down my hallway. And that is 5 stars!
text_fidelity_b: TP-LINK TL-PA511 KIT AV500 Powerline Gigabit Adapter Starter Kit, up to 500Mbps

I've got redundant cloud-based backups set up for my most important data, but I wanted to have a Time Machine backup as well. My Seagate 2TB portable was taking up valuable lap desk real estate (I have to have a graphics tablet handy for design work), so when it crapped out on me, I started looking for something else that might work better.

This little Ultra Fit is working just fine. I had to reformat it for my MacBook Pro, but after I did that, setting up Time Machine was easy. I excluded superfluous non-work items (movies, photos backing up to Google Drive, and my archival book files backing up to pCloud and the SDHC drive), so I can actually get a decent number of backups before Time Machine starts knocking off the older ones. And there's room for me to work on my graphics tablet.

Another reviewer said it's flimsy so best for leaving in place, which is exactly what I'm doing. I haven't had any problems with it so far, and it was a small price to pay for the extra insurance and peace of mind.

They are exactly what they are advertised to be, earbuds with clips that go over the ears to keep them from falling out of your ears when you are engaged in activities that cause a lot of moving and shaking of your head, which would dislodge ordinary earbuds.

I don't personally engage in sports that strenuous, but but I did thoroughly test these Sports Clips by bending over, hopping up and down and generally moving my head a lot. They did not come loose from my ears.

I found another excellent use for them as well. When I have normal earbuds plugged in when I am baking bread or other dishes that get my hands very messy, all too frequently non-clip earbuds begin to slip out of my ears. The one flaw with this product, at least it's a flaw to me, because it doesn't make any sense and is somewhat uncomfortable, is the way the cord is designed. It is not coequal in length on both sides. One side is about four times longer than the other. There also isn't any sliding plastic piece that allows you to adjust the length of the splitting of the cord so that the user can adjust how wide it gaps over one's throat and chest, which would allow the user to opt, as desired, to even tighten it right up under the chin.

Other than those issues, this is an excellent product.

text_fidelity_a: Beyution V4.1 Bluetooth Headphones Wireless Foldable Hi-fi Stereo Headphone for Smart Phones & Tablets - Black I purchased and received these Beyution V4.1 Bluetooth Wireless Foldable Hi-fi Stereo Headphones - Black for $20.99, delivered free with my Prime membership.  This bluetooth receiver, in ear buds or headphones is the best I own or have purchased.  I use them mostly for watching TV, silently in my home living room, early and late.  The are kind of tight fitting on my ears, , but do have soft ear pads.  Each side adjusts an extra inch of fit size and this is adequate for my big round head.  I would recommend them to be folded when they are at their smallest size, as it is kinda flimsy when full opened up.  The controls are on the bottom of the left side; power on/phone button, aux input jack, charge micro usb port, and forward/back/play/pause slide button.  I like them and feel the price with delivery is a pretty good deal.  They sound pretty good when you are listening to Bluetooth, a signal that is not too good for audio fidelity quality, so don't expect plug in quality as a bluetooth receiver.  This headphone can be plugged in and used as a regular cabled set of headphones also.  The bluetooth has the best range of any bluetooth receiver I own.  To hear what they really can sound like, plug them in to the jack and listen to a CD or another high fidelity source, besides MP3, Bluetooth or "Radio" satellite, all sources which are notorious for poor fidelity,  as these are not great HiFi sound signals.  Sound has gone way down hill with these formats for electronics for the masses.  I don't listen to Bluetooth much or these other low fidelity formats with the music I like and if I did, I would prefer to use these headphones, rather than ear buds of similar price.  Of course, much more expensive products can be purchased, but I won't, as I have in the past and they are not worth the investment of my money.

text_fidelity_a:
Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender The tech geek in our household kept telling me there was nothing we could do to improve on the truly horrendous wireless internet service we have. He said we were stuck with the ISP we have and with their router (which he has in the far back bedroom, on the other side of our apartment from the pricey smart TV I haven't been able to use for anything but watching cable news). I haven't been able to stream anything from Amazon Prime, nor can I access the internet at all through the TV. So in complete frustration, without telling him, I ordered the Securifi Almond. Price was one factor in my decision, but I knew I wasn't going to be able to depend on him to help me set anything up and I'm not all that tech savvy.

One of the attractive selling points of this router is that it can be used either as a router or as a range extender. I planned to set it up as a range extender to see if I could get a better signal near my TV, but also had in mind that I might be able to persuade a certain somebody to try it as our router in place of the one that I feel like is defective (or just crummy) from our ISP.

I set it up myself. I just followed the installation on screen, and it was a snap. Fortunately, I knew what our log-in info was for our network so I didn't have to ask for help. I wasn't sure how it was supposed to work with the ethernet cable, so I plugged the Almond into the LAN port of of my TV and into one of the ports with a TV icon on the router. Then I tested it. Wow. The streaming is so much better than it was that I signed up for Netflix and started binging on "House of Cards." I still have the rotating download timer come up once or twice during an episode, but it gets done pretty quickly and the episode finishes playing. Before, I couldn't even load an episode or, worse, it would play a minute then completely drop the connection to the internet.

So I'm quite happy. This is a sleek little baby that works. I can see at a glance that I'm connected, which is reassuring. I haven't yet tried it in its router mode, but as a range extender it works great. You need to use the little stowaway stylus that comes with it when you're selecting onscreen functions, but as long as you remember to re-stow it, you've always got it handy if you need it.
text_fidelity_b: Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender

Accsoon CineEye Video Transmitter, 5G Wireless Live Transmission to 4 Devices, 1080p WiFi HDMI, 100 Meter Range, Supports Android & iOS, RGB, 3D LUT Loading, Incredibly Low Latency – Grey (CineEye) This is a great solution for a remote monitor for video shoots, and it's simple, no wires, no cables, and basically one-button operation. You install the app on your device (iOS or Android), connect the transmitter to your video camera (via HDMI), boot it up, then connect your device to it via WiFi. Launch the app and you're looking live at the video camera output. It delivers 1080p at 60fps and pushes audio to your device too. It's actually pretty awesome.

We gave it a real test in a room full of servers and a lot of potential electronic interference and it delivered a solid signal and connection up to about thirty feet. Beyond that it dropped a frame every now and then, but not bad.

If you're recording video through the app on your device, there's ten-minute limit per file, something to do with restrictions on the app's classification. That doesn't interfere with the camera recording video. It's just a file recording limit on whatever device you're monitoring the video on, if you choose to capture it while you view it.

The build quality is great. It feels practically indestructible. Battery life is solid.

If there is one thing to complain about, it's that the Android app is a bit blah. The iOS version is a lot better.
text_fidelity_b: Accsoon CineEye Video Transmitter, 5G Wireless Live Transmission to 4 Devices, 1080p WiFi HDMI, 100 Meter Range, Supports Android & iOS, RGB, 3D LUT Loading, Incredibly Low Latency – Grey (CineEye)
