If this is your second drive, you can use diskpart to get access to the full 3 gig -- just keep in mind this will erase your entire hard drive. Use it carefully. If it's your primary, your best bet is to partition it before you install Windows. If you aren't very technical, and just need a replacement drive, you're better off picking up a 2 TB, which is the biggest Win 8 can recognize without such additional configuration.

It uses two AA batteries that do not come with the unit. Build quality is very good - better than I expected given the price.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire E 15 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8250U, GeForce MX150, 8GB RAM Memory, 256GB SSD, E5-576G-5762 I am not a gamer, nor do I have 50 internet windows open at once.
I will run between 3-7 programs at once but only 1-2 use much power.
The computer is HEAVY! not for traveling with but it does have a great battery compared to other laptops I have owned. I like the lighted keyboard as I work in the dark often while my husband is watching movies. Some users are bothered by the short light-up time but I am not bothered by tapping a random key to light it up again.
What does bother me, is that I can not allow the computer to go to sleep or close the lid without the fear of the screen not turning back on. The keyboard will light up and the power lights are on but my screen goes black. This issue began shortly before the one-year factory warranty which happened to be right when businesses were closing their doors due to COVID, so it was impossible to talk to anyone in customer service.
When I filed the complaint I received an automated response with very little detail and an address to ship my computer too. Like most others, I need my computer every day and I had no idea how long to expect the computer to be gone for shipping both ways and repair. I also worried they would not see the issue as it wasn't happening too often at first and seems very random. I did not send my laptop. Now the issue happens a lot more and I go to extremes to prevent it from sleeping.
Lesson learned, I will buy all future computers from local stores where my warranty can be handled without shipping mycomputer away for an undetermined amount of time.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire E 15 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8250U, GeForce MX150, 8GB RAM Memory, 256GB SSD, E5-576G-5762

SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46 It just landed in the return envelope today... There has been three major things that led to this:
1) The Vault software stopped responding and started crashing every time I tried to run it. Data inside it were obviously inaccessible. So...
2) I decided to make it brand new and reformat the drive. Using just Windows explorer it did not work (refused), then using disk management - no success, finally using prompt and unconditional formatting (both full and quick) would end up in reporting that disk is not accessible - apparently there is writing protection on it that I could not get passed and it would not allow me to reformat it. So...
3) After attempting to reformat the disk became unreadable and Windows could not see it (disk management would see it as raw partition, not able to format it). Next, I took it off the USB port in order to reinsert it and then I almost burned my finger! This thing was so HOT I could fry an egg on it, if it was bigger! After reinserting into the USB port it would still be unrecognizable.
In short, the disk became a small brick and landed in the return envelope.
Avoid SanDisk as they apparently shovel the write protection down your throat and you can't do anything with your drive later on. So much for your customer flexibility with your product. Rather pick a very similar, ultra-small Samsung USB drive of the same size, also available from Amazon. That one comes clean (i.e. no imposed software nor writing protection) and apparently does not heat at all, or very little compared to this little oven.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Elite 7 Active True Wireless— Bluetooth Sports Earbuds Shake Grip for Secure in-Ear Fit — Ultimate Workout Earbuds, Adjustable Active Noise Cancellation, Fast Charging — Navy I've tried several earbuds from Jabra now, as well as several from most of the major brands, and jabra is consistently my favorite.

Unboxing wasn't especially exciting. Minimalist, but well designed paper packaging with a sheet of quick start instructions that could really use a QR code to save us the trouble of searching for the app and trying to make sure we found the right one.

Getting to the earbud case itself, it's lower and wider than the previous generation earbuds I've tried from them. Opening it up was a treat. The earbuds and whole interior look like some kind of stealth technology. So matte black they absorb light. Pulling them out of the case lights up some tiny LEDs to confirm they are on and battery status. They're coated with something slightly grippy, and although they are held in magnetically, they didn't come out suddenly and make me toss them across the floor like my previous pair. They're a bit smaller and better fitting than the already excellent 85t.

Putting them in, they're quite comfortable. A really good size and fit. Immediately a voice assistant will talk you through pairing, which went smoothly. After locating and installing the app, it alerted me to a firmware update. It took a few minutes, but was as simple as waiting for it to finish while keeping the product near and on. Flashing LEDs keep you apprised of progress. The app has instructions and additional options.

Sound on these is great! I think these are going to be my new favorite earbuds. I've tried the Pro version as well, but I like these better. The Pro seems to just switch out the grippy stealth finish for some improved wind resistance on calls, so usage counts.

Controls are easy and intuitive. A clickable button instead of gesture control, so you can tell what you're doing, and don't trigger it every time you brush the hair away from your ear. They're my favorite way to talk on a cellphone too. Nice to have both hands free.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Elite 7 Active True Wireless— Bluetooth Sports Earbuds Shake Grip for Secure in-Ear Fit — Ultimate Workout Earbuds, Adjustable Active Noise Cancellation, Fast Charging — Navy

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Full Motion Articulating TV Wall Mount Bracket with Swivel and Tilt Features for 32-80 inch TVs and Flat Panels up to 130 Lbs, Black First of all, I'm looking at reviews and pictures of other peoples item and it seems they have a different item, and yet all the reviews are together. Let me start with the good...

PROS_ Inexpensive!

Cons_

THE INSTRUCTIONS: they are written in 6 different languages, and it jumps back and forth between them. It's not broken English, but very hard to follow. Some of them even have a sort of thumbnail of an entire page of text compressed into about 1.5." It is very bizarre. It took about 30 minutes of studying the pictures to figure out what the heck to do, because the manual certainly doesn't tell you. The box comes with sooo much extra hardware to account for different sizes and mounting situations, but the manual does not explain this well.

THE HARDWARE: It is super heavy duty and weighs nearly as much as my TV. My TV is super light weight and is probably 8 or 9 lbs. The bolts that screw into the stud could hold 100lbs I'm sure. Even pre-drilling pilot holes I had difficulty screwing them in with a drill they are so big. It takes so much torque that the screws stripped. I ended up using 1.5" wood screws. I used a stud and I don't like where the TV is mounted, so I am going to get molly bolts to screw it into the drywall where I would like to put it.

NOT STURDY: You mount a plate to the back of the TV, then you mount another piece of hardware to the wall. You then attach the TV to the hardware you just attached to the wall. It is wobbly. It also tilts anywhere from a perfectly neutral position to 20 degree or so angle down. This is in case you are mounting it very high and wish to tilt it down. The TV keeps flopping forward and tilting down. There is a bolt that keeps it in place and I tightened the heck out of it, and it just barely stays put.

NOT FLUSH: I have no other mounting systems to compare it to, but the TV sticks out about 2.5" from the wall. I was expecting it to be much closer.

So there you have it. I am not happy. Ultimately I have the mounted now and no real reason to return it because it's doing what I need it to. There are a lot of positive reviews, but they are I'm sure for a different product. Anyways I paid $15.95. You will most likely be happier with something you pay $25 for.

KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black Overall this keyboard is great. The keys feel nice and they're quiet but not too quiet or soft or squishy. Enjoy typing on this keyboard, pushing the keys seems to take minimal effort and overall it's great.

The best part about the keyboard is that it separates and having the ability to give it a little separation is great. I miss it when I don't have it and it helps avoid torquing the wrists when you are typing. I also love the feel of the keys.

Now before my minor complaints understand two things: (1) I really like this keyboard and despite what I would consider minor defects, I would definitely buy another one. (2) please excuse the fact that I like my keyboards to be consistent and while Apple may not make the *best* keyboards I do use a laptop and I am used to their keyboard layout and feel.

The biggest thing that annoyed me when I purchased this keyboard was the positioning of the ⌘ (command) key. It seems to be shifted over a bit from what I'm used to. Normally I would hit ⌘ with my thumb but it's a little touch to do that on this one given the position of it. It's just something I'm having to get used to.

One minor downside to the keyboard is that the function key doesn't work the same way as the default apple keyboard, rather, the `fn` key is a toggle. I prefer for fn to work as a modifier because that is what I am used to on my laptop keyboard.

Another minor problem is the styling on the caps lock key. Like many people, I remap my caps lock to ctrl and and thus want caps lock to be a normal button. However, on this keyboard the caps lock key is missing the right part of the key so that you don't accidentally hit it when typing the `a` key.

Finally, the escape key and '`' (back tick) keys are in weird positions. The escape key is not as bad as the backtick. There is just something about the distance that I must go that is different from what I'm used to and I have been consistently hitting the `1` key instead. Life goes on.

Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function. Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

After that, it is operating as expected.

Winegard FL-55YR FlatWave Amplified Razor Thin HDTV Indoor Antenna (Renewed) I bought the amped FlatWave refurbished because it was $25 cheaper than a new one, and I am quite pleased with it. It DID come with gunk on it from where the previous owner had taped it up, but the gunked-up side (the black) was the one I placed against the window, facing outside, where nobody is going to see it anyway.

We live in an apartment complex on the outskirts of a city with another apartment building sitting right in front of us where the antenna would face the closest transmission tower. The first time I scanned for channels, I just laid the antenna flat on the table next to the TV. I got 14 channels on that scan (the networks often transmit more than one, so those were ABC, NBC, CBS, and Fox with their variants, one of which was CW). I moved the antenna to the center of my window, which I didn't like the looks of, and got 20 channels when I rescanned, three of which were PBS variants I hadn't gotten before; the rest were shopping channels that I don't care to receive anyway. I moved the antenna over to the side of the window with the cord side up close to the edge of the sill so the cord would hang up against the wall and not look ugly, and I got 17 channels; all I lost were those shopping channels.

We have cable in our bedrooms but none in the living room, so that's where I set up this antenna. I'm hoping I can convince DP to drop cable at some point, because it's ridiculous how much we're paying for it. We could afford to travel some if we could cut back to just internet. But sometimes you just want to be able to watch TV....
text_fidelity_b: Winegard FL-55YR FlatWave Amplified Razor Thin HDTV Indoor Antenna (Renewed)

text_fidelity_a: GMYLE ExpressCard, 34mm to USB 3.0 Dual Port Adapter, Not Support Mac OS Need some USB3 ports on a older MacBook Pro like mine? This card works great on my MacBook Pro 17" 2010 laptop running Mac OS X 10.9 "Mavericks" with the ASMedia USB3 drivers from here: http://www.insanelymac.com/forum/files/download/26-asmedia-usb3/. I rated this purchase less than perfect since I had to find and download these Mac OS X drivers on my own. These drivers do work, because the GMYLE Express USB3.0 Card (model BC628) uses the ASMedia chipset, and some gracious developer added the ASMedia chip signature for this USB ExpressCard to the similar CalDigit USB3.0 Drivers. To install: first download Kext Utility from MacUpdate, then unzip the ASMedia USB3.zip file from the link above, and drag the two .kext files within the zip file to an open Kext Utility window. Another way to install is to download the MultiBeast utility from the same website, http://www.insanelymac.com/.
text_fidelity_b: GMYLE ExpressCard, 34mm to USB 3.0 Dual Port Adapter, Not Support Mac OS

text_fidelity_a: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant Bulbs and outlet are OK. I would not buy separately though, as nowadays you get higher quality bulbs and outlets for a discount price.  The sensor bridge, contact and motion sensors are problematic to say the least. I have 2 contact sensors and 3 motion sensors connected to the sensor bridge. Right now all of them are offline, they started going offline one by one. Distance from the sensors to the bridge is not an issue since two of them are located no more than three feet away from the bridge. This is not the first time this has happened. The only solution for me has been to reset bridge and sensors, and reinstall them one by one. Many people complain about the same issue, and this keeps happening. The camera where the bridge is attached is installed 7 ft from the ground, so it has been very aggravating to have to get a ladder every time one of these switches has gone offline. Regarding the camera, you probably will not find anything cheaper in the market right now. This model in particular offers continuous recording provided you insert a storage card, that is a plus. Person detection is back, however sometimes it takes more than 10 minutes to receive a notification. Some people has reported that it has take up to one hour to get the notification. I personally would not recommend getting this package due to the unreliability of the bridge and motion and contact sensors. This is definitely not a system you want to buy to secure your home. The camera can be purchased separately for about $25. The video quality is acceptable during the daytime. If you want a hobby camera, you will not find a better deal. For security purposes, you are better off looking somewhere else.
text_fidelity_b: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant

text_fidelity_a:
Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue My car is too old to justify installing a bluetooth enabled stereo, and i hate having cords hanging everywhere to use the aux input. This little transmitter did the job, but unfortunately only for about two months.

It's a pain-free setup, and it does work, but I wouldn't buy it again, and I'd recommend a different route should you be in the market for one.

I've tried this in three different vehicles--in all three, the background static you get when it's transmitting is distracting. If it were quiet, I could ignore it but it's enough to interrupt anything I'm listening to. I've tried changing it to a multitude of empty radio stations, even tried it on a fully broadcasting radio station, and the static was horrible regardless.

Secondly, it is a pain in the butt to get out of the ashtray. The directions suggest you unplug it since it can drain your battery, but I had a heck of a time getting it out EVERY time. It had very tight contacts in all vehicles, to the point where if I don't gently wiggle it out, it can (and will) dislocate my ashtray drawer. That's a bit excessive in my opinion, as I've had other ashtray based devices with no tension issues like that.
text_fidelity_b: Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue

Amazon Basics Microphone for Smartphones with Clip - Black This microphone includes a smartphone clip stand. It works fine with my Pixel 2 phone when I connect it to the USB-C dongle cable that was included with my phone. Audio quality is better than phone's built-in microphone, but not as good as the more expensive Shure, Sennheiser, or Audio-Technica microphones that I have used. For voice recording, this microphone is adequate, but for live music performances, I recommend something better. One big advantage of an external microphone is you can aim it at the sound source, instead of relying on whatever direction your phone's microphone is pointing when you aim the camera.

There are a lot of cheap off-brand lavalier microphones on Amazon that work adequately for voice recording, especially at close range. Very hard for me to tell if this one is significantly better than the $10 products.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Microphone for Smartphones with Clip - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker I have owned those annoying bluetooth ear pieces that always feel like they're about to fall off - or actually do. And although the sound varies from product to product, it's just not a system I am comfortable with.

This little speaker is simply perfect for my needs. It is 4 inches by 4 inches wide and only 1 inch thick. It has a switch that you slide to the right when you wish to enable the bluetooth, or to the left to turn it off. There is also another small button right beside the switch that you push in to receive or disconnect a call. A silver volume knob is sleekly incorporated in the overal design. The pairing was instant and consistant. No need to type in some code or wait forever for them to find each other. But here's the most important part - I hear my calls clearly and with no drop off or fade.

In all fairness, I only use this in my car and I don't spend ridiculous amounts of time on my phone when I'm driving. I've used other products with useless results. Half of the time I would risk a ticket by just ditching the ear piece and talking on my cell. In this case, I'm able to place it on the seat next to me and converse without any problems. Now that it's passed my tests, I'll be getting some velcro and mounting it to my dash board when I'm driving, and then just popping it in the glove compartment when I'm done.

The unit comes with a USB charger cable and it had a partial charge when I received it. Once it's fully charged and you turn it on, a blue light will blink for about 2 seconds and then go to a solid blue. According to the enclosed instructions, you will know that the battery is low when it blinks red. Couldn't be easier.

Musically speaking, my JBL and Sony are better designed for that purpose. But as a compact, speaker phone - this Phillips is without equal. Hands-free clarity without an annoying piece of plastic hanging over your ear. What more could you ask?
text_fidelity_b: Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker
